text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 2.64% today, continuing a sharp five-day climb that's seen it gain 7.73% since late September. The immediate catalyst is a widening gap between U.S. and global crude prices—U.S. oil at $96 per barrel versus $113.96 globally—which is highly profitable for refiners like MPC. That $18 spread, combined with refineries running at 92.5% capacity and tight diesel inventories (105 million barrels in storage), means strong margins on fuel production and sales.

The broader backdrop is geopolitical disruption in the Middle East and pressure on global oil supplies. Saudi Aramco warned it could take two years to rebuild global inventories, and ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions are constraining tanker movements and fuel flows. Meanwhile, while the G7 announced diesel stock releases to ease prices, those 100 million barrels will be deployed over four months—a slow trickle that won't immediately ease the supply squeeze that's boosting refiner margins.
